text: Why does `halts` take both a program and an input, rather than just a program?
choices: Because the input determines how much memory the program needs, and memory limits halting.
Halting is a property of the two together — the verified `countdown` halts for positive inputs and not for zero.
Because the proof requires two arguments in order to construct the diagonal.
Because a program with no input always halts, so the case would be trivial otherwise.
explanation: `countdown` decrements before testing for zero, so on input 0 the register goes to -1 and never returns. That is not a bug in the demonstration; it is the interesting case. A program is not simply halting or non-halting, which is why the question must be asked of a pair.
